findings.title: hardcoded-secrets check flat-critical across ~30 secret patterns, double-counts Google keys
findings.summary: Walmart scan: Google API keys matched by generic hardcoded-secrets (severity critical) pushed the whole scan to unsafe/10, despite two dedicated checks (google-api-key-exposed, secret-google-maps-api-key) already correctly rating the same evidence as medium. Client-exposed-by-design keys (Google/Firebase) should not carry the same severity as server-only secrets (AWS/Stripe/DB URIs).
findings.fix: Split hardcoded-secrets into 4 severity-tiered check ids (hardcoded-secrets critical / hardcoded-secrets-high-risk high / hardcoded-secrets-client-exposed medium / hardcoded-secrets-low-risk low) in lib/scanner/checks/code.ts + checks-data/code.json. Removed the Google API Key (AIzaSy*) pattern entirely -- google-api-key-exposed (content.json) and secret-google-maps-api-key/secret-firebase-api-key-public (secrets-extended.json) already cover that evidence at medium/low. Also fixed safety-rating.ts's dead 'Hardcoded API Keys' exploitablePatterns entry (never matched any real title) so the new tiers classify as exploitable-at-their-own-severity instead of falling into 'hardening' or being dropped -- merged with scanner-02's independent fix for the same dead pattern (broader regex, kept as-is). Shipped by agent a9eefbf8ba0b78d5c.

findings.title: Danger score / safety rating ignore AI verification verdicts entirely
findings.summary: getSafetyRating/getDangerScore in lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts weight every finding by severity+title pattern only; a finding the AI already flagged possible_fp counts at full weight, defeating the verification pipeline. Confirmed on Walmart scan: several cookie findings marked possible_fp (detector cited a cookie not present in the live probe) still counted at full weight toward the unsafe/10 verdict.
findings.fix: Extend Finding interface with aiVerdict/aiConfidence, weight accordingly. In progress (agent adf62015a31287147).

findings.title: checkSecurityTxt probes bare apex host, misses www-only security.txt
findings.summary: Walmart scan reported security.txt missing at both well-known/root paths on walmart.com; user manually confirmed www.walmart.com serves a valid security.txt. Apex/www host mismatch in lib/scanner/async-checks.ts's checkSecurityTxt, likely a redirect-handling or origin-source bug.
findings.fix: Root-causing redirect/origin handling. In progress (agent a4a7418e77b0d7ded).

findings.title: AI verification timeout/chunk-size too tight for realistic finding counts
findings.summary: lib/ai/verify-findings.ts's verifyInChunks stops at a 90s total deadline with chunk size 5; only ~35-40 of Walmart's 57 findings received an AI verdict before the deadline hit, the rest silently unverified with no coverage indicator.
findings.fix: Increasing CONFIG_AI_VERIFY_TOTAL_TIMEOUT_MS/CHUNK_SIZE with worst-case arithmetic, checking client-side timeout parity. In progress (agent a567911127be41393).

findings.title: Discord sign-in/sign-up redirect URI never documented for registration
findings.summary: The unified sign-in/sign-up OAuth flow added in app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/ redirects to /api/v3/auth/oauth/discord/callback for Discord, a distinct URI from the older Profile > Connections linking flow's /api/v3/auth/discord/callback. .env.example (and the operator's own .env.local) only ever documented the older URI for the Discord Developer Portal. A self-hoster (or this SaaS's own Discord app, if registered before the unified flow existed) who followed that doc registers only one of the two required redirect URIs, so the Sign in with Discord / Sign up with Discord buttons on /login and /signup -- which render whenever DISCORD_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are set, per /api/v3/auth/oauth/info -- fail at Discord with a redirect_uri mismatch, while the Profile Connect button keeps working. Same bug class as cc1b1f9f's GitHub repo-connect fix earlier today, but Discord's two flows are intentionally separate (not merged), so the fix is registering both URIs rather than consolidating callbacks.
findings.fix: Documented both required OAuth2 redirect URLs in the Discord Developer Portal section of .env.example -- confirm the production/sandbox Discord app also has both registered.
